target_customer: Businesses and developers that need to test, manage and deploy VR and AR apps to many devices
problem: Companies had no simple way to distribute and manage VR and AR apps at scale, so ConstructVR offered a platform to test, manage and deploy them.
business_model: Software platform for enterprise VR and AR app distribution (pricing not stated in sources)
product_category: VR and AR app deployment platform

founders.name: Chris Tan
prior_employers: Enterprise software client work for Wells Fargo and Verizon (per YC page bio)
previous_startups: Described on the YC page as a technical YC alumnus with CEO experience; earlier company not named

competitors.name: InsiteVR
competitors.what: YC W15 company that turns 3D models into VR walkthroughs for design and construction, an adjacent VR enterprise tool

technical_complexity.rationale: Pushing builds to headsets and phones across fragmented 2016 VR platforms needed device management work, but no hard research problem.

defensibility.rationale: No data, integrations or customers are documented, and device management vendors could add VR support.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later sources show purpose built XR management (ManageXR, ArborXR) and MDM vendors serving the need, but none is shown to have copied ConstructVR.

market_need_then: A 2016 Enterprisers Project piece said enterprise VR and AR interest was growing but convincing use cases were scarce. A HackerNoon post of August 2016 listed ConstructVR among enterprise VR distribution platforms in the Summer 2016 YC era.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand; a later unrelated company reuses the same name and creates confusion.

outcome_analysis: ConstructVR was a two person YC Winter 2016 team building VR and AR app deployment tools. A Product Hunt launch in June 2016 is recorded by a search summary, and the YC page now lists it inactive. No shutdown notice, funding or press explains the outcome, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: The company website safety check was rate limited so constructvr.io was not read. Crunchbase and VCBacked pages showed no amounts and an Altss page says investment data is gated; nothing is recorded as a round. Founding year: YC says 2015, Seedtable says 2016. The InsiteVR source is dated about five months after the batch and is adjacent rather than a direct rival, so treat the competitor list as thin. A Persana blog describes a different company with the same name founded in 2022 and is not used.
